criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a drain test with three queued items where a newer item is planned first shows the drain works items in plan order, not oldest first.
criteria.evidence: The test `items_are_worked_in_plan_order_not_oldest_first` passed. It queues a, b, c with c the newest and on a higher rung, and b depending on a. It checks that items are read in the order c, a, b, and that the groups are [c, a] then [b].

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a drain test that requests a stop mid-run shows the loop finishes the current job, starts no further job, and reports a distinct stop reason (not a killed job).
criteria.evidence: The test `a_stop_asked_for_mid_run_finishes_the_current_job_and_starts_no_other` passed. The stop is set while job a runs. The log is exactly read a, run a, land a, rate. The stop reason is Stop::Requested, a's landing is 'landed', and b and c stay queued. A second test, `a_stop_asked_for_before_any_job_starts_runs_nothing`, also passed.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a plan built from several open items names, for each, goal, ladder rung, acceptance, open questions, dependencies, and touched paths, and groups items with disjoint touches and no dependency as parallel while ordering dependent items after what they need.
criteria.evidence: PlanEntry has all six fields. `disjoint_independent_items_share_a_group_and_dependents_come_after` passed: [base, docs] form one group, clash (which overlaps base's paths) gets its own group, and after (which needs base) comes later. The reading test `an_unread_request_is_planned_from_its_own_words_and_a_read_one_from_its_reading` checks that goal, acceptance, touches, depends_on and rung are filled from the request. It does not assert open_questions.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: an item whose plan lacks goal, ladder rung, or acceptance is refused for design or code and reported, so planning cannot be skipped.
criteria.evidence: The drain test `an_item_whose_plan_lacks_goal_rung_or_acceptance_is_not_worked_and_is_reported` passed: only d is read, run and landed. a, b and c are refused with goal, ladder rung and acceptance missing, stay queued, and the report shows 'the plan lacks acceptance'. The unit test `a_plan_without_goal_rung_or_acceptance_is_refused` also passed.

criteria.criterion: The plan-stage audit from n2qb is described: each logged gap (intervention, introspection, rejection, rating) is traced to a stage (reading, decomposition, assumptions, criteria, outcome check), with a check of whether later gaps of that kind fell; if full automation is too large, the remainder is stated as follow-up.
criteria.evidence: Checked by reading. plan.rs has GapKind (four kinds), Stage (five stages), trace() and GapLog::fell(), with tests. roles-and-ladder.md has a section 'The plan-stage audit (first slice)', and D105 and CHANGELOG describe it too. The follow-up is stated: reading gaps from records, a report in status, and a role that proposes stage changes.

criteria.criterion: Docs (README, design doc, CHANGELOG) state the planning-first order and how to stop a drain at a job boundary, for an outside reader.
criteria.evidence: Checked by reading. README has two new paragraphs, 'Planning comes first' and 'Stopping a drain', which tell the reader to run `athena drain-stop` from another terminal and contrast it with `athena stop`. roles-and-ladder.md and CHANGELOG (Changed and Added entries) cover both. The doc claims match the code: drain.rs checks stop_file(), main.rs clears a stale stop file when drain starts, and exit code 2 holds for any stop other than target met.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check: all pass, and no new unused or untested module.
criteria.evidence: clippy and fmt --check passed. The full cargo test run finished, but its output went to a file outside my working directory that I was not allowed to read. Athena's own run of the same command passed with 734 tests, and my targeted runs passed (41 drain tests, 8 plan/reading tests). The new module plan.rs is used by drain.rs and has 7 unit tests.

criteria.criterion: No design work for moving compute to CI is included; it is left for after this lands.
criteria.evidence: Checked by reading. No file in the diff touches CI or routing. D105 says explicitly that moving compute to CI comes after this change and is not part of it.

findings.summary: A file outside the expected deliverables was changed.
findings.evidence: The diff adds lines to display.rs that print plan groups and refusals in the drain text report. display.rs is not on the deliverables list. The change is small and the drain tests depend on it.

findings.summary: The refusal gate rarely fires on real requests.
findings.evidence: RealSteps gives every job a rung, defaulting to Implementation, so 'ladder rung' is never missing. plan_entry uses an unread request's first line as its acceptance, so only an empty request is refused. D105's tradeoff section says this openly.

findings.summary: The audit's tracing and before/after check are not used anywhere outside tests yet.
findings.evidence: No code outside tests calls plan::trace or GapLog. The docs state that wiring them to the records is follow-up.

findings.summary: Open questions are filled in but no test checks them.
findings.evidence: The test asserts goal, acceptance, touches, depends_on and rung, but not open_questions.

summary: I read the full diff and ran the tests myself. Drain now works the queue in the order a plan sets: higher ladder rung first, a dependent item after what it needs, and age only to break ties. The report lists groups of items that could run in parallel, though drain still runs one job at a time. An item whose plan has no goal, rung or acceptance is refused and reported. A new `athena drain-stop` command writes a stop file in the state directory. Drain checks it before each job, so the current job is finished, landed and rated, and drain ends with the new stop reason `stop requested`. The first slice of the n2qb audit is a function that traces a gap to a stage and a check of whether later gaps fell; it is in code and tests, and the follow-up is stated. README, the design doc, CHANGELOG and decision D105 (which lists alternatives) describe all of this. Results I saw: 41 drain tests and 8 plan/reading unit tests pass, clippy is clean and the fmt check passes. The full cargo test run finished, but its saved output was outside my working directory so I could not read the totals; I rely on Athena's own run (734 passed) for that. All results are about this snapshot only. The change contains no work on moving compute to CI. Three minor findings: `display.rs` changed but is not on the deliverables list; the refusal gate rarely fires in real use, because every job gets a default rung and an unread request's first line counts as its acceptance (D105 admits this); and the audit code is not yet called outside tests.
